fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 does not specify how finite-field evaluations, modular syndromes, carries, pair/triple selectors, targets, and weights become one unrestricted Euclidean CVP instance. If it retains the complete G14 pair-bag system, repeating the already-passed B+32 shell is not discriminating; if it replaces that system, the exact replacement is undefined, and deterministic selector lifts remain vulnerable to G13/G15 affine lifting.

Proposal 2 cannot underlie a polynomial-time reduction by first computing a Nullstellensatz refutation of the input NO instance. Emitting all Macaulay rows avoids that computation only at a degree whose monomial count and coefficient complexity must be uniformly polynomial; the proposed three-variable certificate experiment cannot discriminate this asymptotic blocker.

Proposal 3 supplies no explicit reduction from clauses to transports, prescribed holonomies, ACCEPT condition, matched control, objective, or shell bound. Multiplication-table and sheet selectors linearize the nonabelian product into a signed finite-state chain, leaving the same representation/splicing danger concretely exhibited by G19.

Proposal 4 relies on quadratic rank-one conditions: 2x2 minors are not CVP-linear constraints. Introducing pair selectors does not enforce products over unrestricted integers, and the resulting pseudotensor relaxation is exposed to G13-style affine combinations; moreover its seed is the G28 rule whose measured illegal growth was already below legal growth.

Proposal 5 cannot force a canonical residue range using only linear one-hot, quotient, and carry equations on unrestricted integer coefficients. Affine combinations of complete deterministic residue encodings preserve every such row, while the proposed G7-only shell omits the stronger verified G13 affine collision and G15 lift.

Proposal 6 is not outside the signed-flow obstruction: length-three windows are ordinary first-order flow on the de Bruijn graph whose vertices are length-two windows. Restricting edges to a nonlinear recurrence changes the graph but not the linear signed-flow relaxation, and no exact scan, acceptance rows, control, or radius is frozen.

Proposal 7 tests two satisfiable overlapping OR clauses rather than an unsatisfiable soundness obstruction and leaves the deep hole, truth cosets, glue code, target, weights, and shell unspecified. Outer-code distance helps only after a nonzero discriminant syndrome; it does not address a G13 affine lift with zero syndrome.

Across all seven proposals, a constant-fixture shell pass would remain finite evidence and none supplies a uniform polynomial-size construction, composition invariant, or dimension-dependent gap law. Scaling residual rows after a finite no-kernel audit cannot promote that audit to asymptotic soundness.
evidence: G13 verifies an exact integral affine combination of 16 globally consistent encodings that annihilates every compatible raw-selector linear syndrome over several primes.

G15 verifies that the same affine coefficients lift through every node of an enlarged deterministic hierarchy with exactly zero residual, showing that nonlinear naming followed by linear selector compilation is not automatically an escape.
G19 finds an exact accepting signed flow with two negative coefficients despite nonlinear ordered-product semantics, directly undermining the holonomy and higher-window arguments.
G14 already proves the complete pair-bag obstruction empty through B+32, while G28 subsequently shows that a finite pair-based pass need not compose: lambda=57/32 is below mu=2.

G7 and G11 exhibit exact zero-residual signed selector kernels; G12 shows that charging one kernel can merely expose a cheaper clause drop. The supplied status explicitly establishes no hardness lemma or dimension-dependent gap.
next_experiment: None authorized. Reopen only a separately preregistered mutation giving the complete emitted CVP basis, target, matched YES/NO instances, coefficient bound, shell radius, and acceptance threshold, together with explicit G13 affine-lift and G19 signed-flow audits; a constant instance must test a new obstruction rather than repeat G14.
